receipt.public_excerpt: Patients who use AI to guide health care decisions assume potential risks.

evidence_items.explanation: Five emergency physicians evaluated answers from ChatGPT 3.5, Google Bard, Bing AI Chat, and Claude AI to ten emergency-care questions. Reported failures included omitting life-threatening diagnoses and unsafe emergency instructions, supporting the inference that acting on these answers could endanger life; the study did not measure actual injuries.

evidence_items.locator: Abstract, Conclusions; Results and Plain language summary
evidence_items.explanation: In a controlled chest-pain vignette study involving 50 physicians, GPT-4 assistance improved decision accuracy in both patient demographic groups. This limits any inference that LLM involvement necessarily worsens care, but physician assistance in one scenario does not establish the safety of delegating life-critical decisions.

unresolved_gaps: The evaluations do not determine whether the absence of explicit world models explains the failures.
They do not estimate actual deaths, population-level risk, or the net effect of LLM use compared with existing care.
The emergency-care evaluation tested a small set of questions and older chatbot versions; it cannot establish identical risk across all systems available at the post date.
